Chang) What is the largest possible number of solutions of the equation x2 1 + x2 2 = x2 3 + x2 where the variables x1; : : :; x4 attain values from an integer set A with prescribed size? In [18] it is shown that this number of solutions is O(jAj3=(ln jAj)1=12), which readily implies that for any nite set S of squares one has jS + Sj jSj(ln jSj)1=12 (cf. Prob- lem 4.6). It is also conjectured in [18] that for any xed " > 0 the number of solutions is O(jAj2+") (with the implicit constant depending on ").

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers, and let $N$ denote its cardinality. Consider the number $E(A)$ of quadruples $(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4) \in A^4$ satisfying
$$x_1^2 + x_2^2 = x_3^2 + x_4^2.$$

(a) Determine the largest possible value of $E(A)$, as a function of $N$, taken over all integer sets $A$ with $|A| = N$. It is known that $E(A) = O\bigl(N^3 / (\ln N)^{1/12}\bigr)$.

(b) (Conjecture.) Prove or disprove that for every fixed $\varepsilon > 0$ one has
$$E(A) = O_\varepsilon\bigl(N^{2+\varepsilon}\bigr),$$
with implicit constant depending only on $\varepsilon$.

Equivalently (for part (b)), show that for every finite set $S$ of perfect squares and every $\varepsilon > 0$,
$$|S+S| \gg_\varepsilon |S|^{2-\varepsilon}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a well-known open question in additive combinatorics attributed to M.-C. Chang concerning the additive energy of a set of squares. The best known upper bound remains of the form $|A|^3 / (\ln|A|)^c$ for a small constant $c$, far from the conjectured $|A|^{2+\varepsilon}$. No search result indicates a resolution of the conjecture.
